# `format_emmc`

<!-- Generated by tools/gen_cards.py from catalog/. Do not edit by hand. -->

Reformat the internal memory (exFAT), recreate the default directories and clear the favourites database.

## Summary

| Item | Value |
|---|---|
| Kind | method (client sends) |
| Grade | MUTATOR / established (64-bit build; 32-bit build probable) |
| Side-effect tier | C |
| Confidence | READ |
| Basis | static analysis of firmware 9.31, handler @0xc2730 (64-bit build), FormatStorage @0xb2330 |

No request parameters are read and there is no confirmation parameter, mode guard or park/capture guard. The handler checks that the model has internal memory, disables the file-sharing service, force-unmounts the internal volume, formats it as exFAT with the volume label Seestar, remounts it, recreates the default directories, takes a storage snapshot, clears the favourites database and re-enables file sharing (the last step is run whenever the disable step succeeded, whatever happened in between). The shell step runs to completion with no timeout. Partial destructive work can precede an error. A volume whose size query fails appears in the snapshot without any of the size members. Observable storage and file-sharing changes may be announced by separate hotplug events; which ones is unresolved.

Side effects: Destroys all data on the internal memory, remounts it, recreates default directories, clears the favourites database and briefly disables file sharing.

## Request params

| Name | Type | Required | Default | Notes |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| `id` | any | yes | - | Client-chosen request identifier, echoed in the reply as parsed (same JSON type). Required; a request without one is rejected with code 200. The device accepts any JSON value: zero, negative, string, null, boolean and composite ids are all treated as real requests, not notifications. Clients SHOULD use an integer or a string and SHOULD keep ids unique among outstanding requests. On early dispatcher errors (100, 200) the reply carries id null. [READ] |
| `method` | string | yes | - | Fixed value `"format_emmc"`. [READ] |
| `params` | any | no | - | Not read. Omission, null, object, scalar and array all take the same path. Clients SHOULD omit it. [READ] |

## Reply

| Name | Type | Required | Default | Notes |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| `jsonrpc` | string | no | - | (error) Added by the socket layer (reply object constructor), not the handler fragment. Normally present; absent on a stop_func relay-failure reply. Receivers MUST NOT require it. Fixed value `"2.0"`. [READ; also OBSERVED on the wire (2026-10-12)] |
| `Timestamp` | string | no | - | (error) Decimal string `<seconds>.<nanoseconds>` with exactly nine fractional digits, formatted with `%ld.%09ld` from clock_gettime clock id 1. Linux clock id 1 is CLOCK_MONOTONIC, so the value is monotonic time, not wall-clock or Unix time (INFERRED from the clock id). On replies it is added by the socket layer and is normally present; receivers MUST NOT require it on replies (absent on a stop_func relay-failure reply). On events it is always written by the event constructor. [READ; wire shape also OBSERVED (2026-10-12)] |
| `method` | string | if the request had an id and a string method (handler errors and 103), except a locally built stop_func relay failure | - | (error) The request method, echoed. Absent on dispatcher errors 100 and 200 and on a stop_func relay failure. [READ] |
| `error` | string | yes | - | (error) Message looked up from the code; unknown codes yield "fail to operate". [READ] |
| `code` | integer | yes | - | (error) Nonzero. A requested code of 0 is coerced to 207. [READ] |
| `id` | any | yes | - | (error) The request id echoed with its JSON type; null on dispatcher errors 100 and 200, where it is the only way to recognise the reply and cannot be matched to a request. [READ] |

## Errors

| Code | Trigger | Label |
|---|---|---|
| 210 | The model has no internal memory | `not supported` |
| 207 | Disabling file sharing failed, or the captured format command output contains the substring error | `fail to operate` |
| 214 | The shell command could not be started | `fail to run command` |
| 531 | Clearing the favourites database failed | `operate database fail` |
| 200 | Dispatcher: request has no id | `invalid id` |
| 100 | Dispatcher: method missing or not a string | `invalid request` |

A nonzero exit status of the shell command is not itself an error. Lower-level file-sharing errors beyond its boolean result are unresolved.

## Example

Request, format:

```json
{"id":41,"method":"format_emmc"}
```

Reply, ok:

```json
{"jsonrpc":"2.0","Timestamp":"1234.123456789","method":"format_emmc","result":{"is_typec_connected":false,"connected_storage":["emmc"],"storage_volume":[{"name":"emmc","state":"mounted","total_mb":57000,"totalMB":57000,"free_mb":56900,"freeMB":56900,"disk_mb":57000,"diskSizeMB":57000,"used_percent":1}],"cur_storage":"emmc"},"code":0,"id":41}
```

Reply, error:

```json
{"jsonrpc":"2.0","Timestamp":"1234.123456789","method":"format_emmc","error":"not supported","code":210,"id":42}
```
